hints: Notice the given absolute uncertainties: $\pm 0.1 \text{ g}$ in $m = 6.2 \text{ g}$, $\pm 0.1 \text{ cm}$ in $l = 25.0 \text{ cm}$ and $\pm 0.01 \text{ mm}$ in $d = 2.00 \text{ mm}$.
Recall that for $\rho = 4m/(\pi d^2 l)$ the percentage uncertainties add, but any quantity raised to a power $n$ contributes $n$ times its percentage, so $d^2$ contributes twice.
Calculate $100 \times 0.1/6.2$, $100 \times 0.1/25.0$ and $100 \times 0.01/2.00$ separately, double the last one, then add all three.
walkthrough: Write the rule for this product and quotient: percentage uncertainty in $\rho$ = percentage uncertainty in $m$ + percentage uncertainty in $l$ + $2 \times$ percentage uncertainty in $d$, because $\rho$ is proportional to $m^1 l^{-1} d^{-2}$.
Calculate each basic percentage: for mass $100 \times 0.1/6.2 \approx 1.61\%$, for length $100 \times 0.1/25.0 = 0.40\%$, for diameter $100 \times 0.01/2.00 = 0.50\%$.
Allow for the square: the diameter appears as $d^2$, so its contribution is $2 \times 0.50\% = 1.00\%$. Constants $4$ and $\pi$ have no uncertainty.
Add the contributions: $1.61\% + 0.40\% + 1.00\% \approx 3.01\%$, which rounds to $3.0\%$.
